findings.text: The intercept query helper collects repetition prefix, decoded modrm pieces, source and destination values with sizes and kinds, address size, and current plus next instruction pointers into a temporary descriptor, then forwards that descriptor with the requested intercept and stage to the operation table intercept routine and returns its outcome.

General register access is cached per context. A read validates the index, reports misuse through the bug helper and folds out of range values, lazily pulls missing entries from the operation table read routine and marks them valid. A write handle marks the slot both valid and dirty after compile time size checks. A read modify write handle ensures the value is loaded before exposing a mutable slot.

The bug check helper evaluates its condition once, emits a once only warning on truth, notifies the operation table that virtual state is tainted, and yields truthiness so callers can take a fallback path such as masking an index. It must not be treated as fatal on its own.

Effective and stack addresses are truncated by width. An address size derived mask keeps only low bits for narrow modes, register values pass through that truncation, stack pointer updates preserve unmasked high bits, the stack mask is all ones in 64 bit mode and otherwise derived from the stack segment size attribute to yield 16 or 32 bit wrapping, and the stack width in bytes is derived from the highest set bit of that mask.

Fault reporting funnels through a single routine that rejects vectors above 31 as unhandleable, otherwise records vector, error code and validity flag in the context exception record and requests fault propagation. Small wrappers select debug, general protection, stack, invalid opcode, segment not present, divide, and device not available cases, with only some carrying an error code and debug also storing a debug status value.

Segment and address helpers isolate mode effects. The base is forced to zero for low numbered segments in 64 bit mode and otherwise taken from the cached base operation. Descriptor limits are expanded when granularity is set. Selector readers preserve descriptor content while selector writers preserve descriptor and extension base. Virtual width is 57 bits when the LA57 flag in CR4 is set else 48, and noncanonical testing delegates to the operation table canonical check.

Linear address formation adds segment base to effective address then validates by mode. In 64 bit mode the sum is untagged through the operation table, checked for canonical form against virtual width, and bounded by remaining space to the top with oversize rejected. In legacy modes the segment must be usable, code or read only versus write and unreadable code versus non fetch accesses are rejected, expand down segments invert the limit check, the effective address must stay within scaled limit, and remaining length caps the access. Misalignment diagnosed from descriptor flags faults as general protection, while base failures on the stack segment fault as stack errors and others as general protection.

Memory access entry points separate translation from transfer. One helper translates with a write indication derived from a boolean. Segmented standard readers and writers translate then call the operation table standard read or write with the context exception record and a non system indication. Linear system readers and writers skip translation and call the same table with a system indication.

Processor mode and instruction pointer form a small state machine. Mode is recomputed from protection enable, virtual 8086 flag, long mode active, and code segment size attributes to select real, virtual 8086, 16, 32, or 64 bit modes, rejecting long mode active combined with real or virtual 8086 or missing code segment as unhandleable. Instruction pointer assignment truncates to operand width, revalidates as a fetch from the code segment, and commits the new value only on success. Near assignment and relative jumps keep the mode, far assignment recomputes mode first.

Instruction bytes are fetched in bounded chunks from the code segment. A probe with zero length obtains the translatable maximum without boundary enforcement, then the implementation caps to the 15 byte total instruction budget, the segment maximum, and the remainder of the current page. If the capped amount cannot satisfy the newly needed bytes the emulation faults as general protection, noting that only two pages can straddle because one page is preloaded. Otherwise the operation table fetch routine appends bytes and advances the fetch end. A fast path avoids the slow probe when buffered bytes suffice, and fetch helpers advance the decoded pointer and instruction pointer while copying out.

Register operand decoding distinguishes vector and scalar forms. With AVX and 32 byte operand size it selects a 256 bit vector slot and loads host state, with AVX or SSE it selects a 128 bit slot and loads host state, with MMX it masks the index to eight entries and selects an 8 byte slot, otherwise it selects a general register with byte width when the byte operation flag is set. General register selection honors the high byte alias for indices four through seven only without REX and with byte operations, and scalar values are captured in both current and original fields at the operand width.

ModRM decoding extends register fields with REX bits, splits mode, register, and memory fields, defaults the data segment, and takes a register path for register direct mode or when modification is disabled. Sixteen bit addressing combines base and index registers with 8 or 16 bit displacements or direct address, selects stack segment for base patterns involving base pointer, and wraps to 16 bits. Thirty two and 64 bit addressing decodes scale index base bytes with scaled index addition, 32 bit displacement for missing base or direct modes, stack segment selection for stack pointer or base pointer bases, and an operand size adjustment for stack pointer pop forms.

Descriptor table operands are read as a two byte size followed by an address whose width maps two to three, advancing the effective address between reads. Bit scan forward and reverse suppress destination writeback by marking the destination absent when the source is zero while still running the underlying emulation to update flags. Condition testing masks to four bits before delegating to the shared condition evaluator.

Host floating point state is guarded by a paired acquire and release. Acquisition locks the floating point register set, asserts state consistency, and ensures the current thread state is loaded. Release unlocks. All host x87 and vector accesses in this lane bracket their work between acquisition and release, and vector read wrappers perform acquisition around the raw register move.

x87 initialization and status or control stores first inspect task switched and emulation flags in CR0 and raise a device not available fault when either is set. Otherwise they acquire host floating point state, perform the host operation, release, and for stores place the 16 bit result into the destination value while reporting continuation.

Raw vector readers dispatch on index zero through fifteen with upper indices available only on 64 bit builds and treat any other index as a fatal bug. Wrapped readers add floating point locking around the raw move. A separate fault safe execution helper reports unhandleable when the attempted operation faults and continuation otherwise, so callers must handle the unhandleable path.

Observed architectural limits include a 15 byte maximum instruction fetch window, a 16 byte alignment requirement for the 16 byte aligned case with smaller sizes defaulting to byte alignment, rejection of exception vectors above 31, virtual address widths of 48 or 57 bits selected by LA57, stack wrapping at 16, 32, or 64 bits, and operand widths of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32 bytes for scalar and vector forms.

Observed emulator state includes general register cache with validity and dirty bitmasks and backing storage, decode fields for repetition prefix, REX, opcode, modrm pieces, operand and address sizes, mode, flags, and descriptor bits, source and destination operands with type, width, address union, current and original values plus vector halves, 64 bit instruction pointers for commit and decode, an exception record with vector, error code and validity plus debug status, a fetch window with base, cursor, and end, and segmented addresses as segment plus effective address.
